title: The Desert Lake That Won't Dry Up — Silk Road EP2 | China Travel Expert
description:
There is a crescent-shaped lake in the middle of a Chinese desert that refuses to dry up.

This is Crescent Lake (Yueyaquan), 6km south of Dunhuang in Gansu, cupped inside the dunes of Mingsha — the "Singing Sand" Mountain. The desert loses roughly 2,400mm of water to evaporation each year and receives only about 50mm of rain, yet the spring has survived for centuries and is called the "First Spring in the Deserts." The dunes around it rise some 250m and hum when the wind moves the sand. Silk Road caravans rested at this same oasis on the road west.

🧭 Expert Tip: Climb the dunes for sunrise — the sand is cool, the light is soft, and you skip the fierce midday desert heat.

沙漠中央一弯月牙泉，蒸发2400毫米、降水50毫米，却千年不涸。
